description: Two pages give incompatible accounts of how PAM authentication reaches Couchbase Server. security-management-overview.md lists three peer mechanisms: 'authentication-mechanisms based on _Native LDAP_, _saslauthd_, and _PAM_ can be used'. configure-pam.md's own procedure contradicts the peer framing in its prerequisites, instructing the administrator to 'verify that `saslauthd` is set up to use PAM' - so PAM is reached THROUGH saslauthd, not alongside it. authentication-domains.md states the dependency in a parenthesis: '(Note that `saslauthd` also provides support of legacy PAM-based authentication.)' This matters more than a wording preference, because the same page states that Native LDAP and saslauthd are mutually exclusive - 'The two cannot be used simultaneously' - and if PAM requires saslauthd then choosing Native LDAP silently rules PAM out too. Under the three-peer framing that consequence is invisible, and it is the question an administrator planning external authentication actually needs answered.
note: The registry records the dependency rather than the peer framing: idp:pam's type field says PAM is 'delivered through saslauthd rather than natively', on the strength of configure-pam.md's own prerequisite. If an SME confirms PAM can be used without saslauthd on some path, the registry record is the thing to correct, not just the docs.
